g.text: 05 / A FEW NOTES FROM THE JOURNEY
I’m drawn to the whole path from a question to a
working application. A dataset invites an
experiment; an experiment raises new
questions; an interface gives someone else a
way to explore the result. That connection
between investigation and implementation is
what keeps me interested in applied machine
learning, computer vision, and software
development.
My projects give me different ways to practice
that approach. Retinal-imaging experiments
bring together inference and visual
explanations. Local language-model
comparisons make room for response analysis
and error inspection. Security and recognition
labs turn technical decisions into workflows that
can be explored step by step. Across these
areas, I’m learning to explain what a system
does, what its results mean, and where its limits
begin.
Alongside those experiments, I’m strengthening
the foundations that make them easier to build
and maintain: data structures, algorithms,
databases, APIs, and application design. I want
each project to leave me with a clearer
understanding of the problem, better questions
for the next iteration, and documentation that
helps another person follow the work.
